description: Performance controller that switches a sequencer's pattern on the beat: an expander queues the next pattern and this module changes to it on the next Advance trigger, putting out the pattern CV

params.text: Sets how many patterns the sequencer being driven has, 2 to 128; the pattern CV is worked out from it, so a wrong setting selects the wrong pattern
Sets the voltage the sequencer expects for its highest pattern, 0V to 10V; the pattern CV is spread across that span
Sets how many of those patterns may be switched to, which is what the expanders offer
Sets the pattern the module jumps to on a reset, when the toggle beside it is on
Turns the reset-pattern jump on and off
Sends a reset by hand: it fires the reset output, and jumps to the reset pattern if that is switched on
Advances by hand: whatever the expanders have queued is switched to at once
Chooses a pattern to switch to by hand, which the button beside it then applies
Switches to the pattern the knob beside it has chosen, without waiting for an Advance trigger

inputs.text: The sequencer's clock on its way through; it is held back by a couple of samples so the reset reaches the sequencer first
A rise past 2V switches to whatever pattern is queued
A rise past 2V resets the module, which sends a trigger to the reset output and, if that option is on, jumps to the reset pattern

outputs.text: The clock from the CLOCK input, delayed by the number of samples the menu sets, and with the first clock after a reset optionally dropped
A 10V pulse when the module is reset and again whenever the pattern changes; patch it to the sequencer so it starts its new pattern in the right place
The voltage the sequencer needs to select the current pattern, worked out from the pattern count and the CV range

notes: the module does nothing on its own: it needs one of its expanders placed touching it on the right, and a trigger source patched to the Advance input
with a phasor-driven sequencer, send the phasor straight to it rather than through the clock jacks; the reset output can be used to restart the phasor
every jack is monophonic, whatever is patched in
menu: Pattern output offset — a slider adding a share of one pattern step to the pattern CV, which lines the module up with sequencers that read the voltage differently
Clock delay — a slider setting how many samples the clock is held back by, 0 to 50, at 2 to begin with
Ignore first clock within 1ms after reset — drops the first clock arriving immediately after a reset, which many sequencers need to stay in step

inputs.0: high above 2V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.1: high above 2V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.2: high above 2V · stepped · one channel only
